summary: Natasha Reichle works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She completed her dissertation at the University of California, Berkeley under doctoral supervisor Joanna Gottfried Williams, also studying with Amin Sweeney, Lewis Lancaster, Patricia Berger, Jeffrey Alan Hadler, and Ninik Lunde.
Natasja Bosma is an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Groningen between circa 2013 and 2018, supervised by Hans T. Bakker.

Nathan Sivin (1931-2022) was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology who studied at the Defense Language Institute, MIT, Kyoto University, and Harvard. He held faculty posts at MIT (1966-1977) and the University of Pennsylvania (1977-2006).

Nathan W. Hill is a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and sinology who studied at Harvard (~2001-2006) under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp and Jay Jasanoff. He held posts at SOAS (~2008-2019) and Trinity College Dublin (from ~2019).

Nathaniel Brassey Halhed (1751-1830) was an Indologist and linguist who was educated at Harrow School and Christ Church, Oxford. He served as an official for the East India Company from circa 1771 to 1785.

Nathaniel DeWitt Garson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Jeffrey Hopkins and also studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Namdrol.
Nathaniel Grove works in Tibetology and computational studies. He held posts at the University of Virginia, where he was attested in 2006 and as a Research Associate in 2026.

Nathaniel Tarn (1928-2024) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Cambridge, Paris, and Chicago. He held academic posts at LSE (~1953-1954), SOAS (~1963-1967), Princeton (1970), and Rutgers University (1972-1985).

Nathmal Tatia was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned a Doctor of Literature at the University of Calcutta under Satkari Mookerjee and Sukhlal Sanghvi. He served as Director of the Jain Vishva Bharati Institute (attested 1982-1990).
Navina Lamminger is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Munich under the supervision of Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Ngawang Thokmey works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as South Asian bibliographer at the University of Virginia (attested 2003-2008) and as Assistant Professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

Nawang Tsering is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under doctoral supervisor Lal Mani Joshi. He served as a lecturer at the Central Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1985).
Neal Donner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz (attested 1976).
Neelima Mundayar is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She is a PhD student at the University of Edinburgh, studying under doctoral supervisor Wilfried Swenden (attested 2026).

Nenghai Shi (1886-1967) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Peking University and under teachers including Kecheng Zhang and Khangsar Rinpoche. He served as vice-president of the Buddhist Association of China (1953-1966).
Ng-Fung Yuen is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of the West under doctoral supervisor Kottegoda Warnasuriya (attested 2009).
Ngakchang Gönpo Tsé Ten studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Ngan-che Chan is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Jing Yin (attested 2007) and also studied under K. L. Dhammajoti.
Ngawang Jinpa is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery. He served as a professor at St. Joseph's College, Darjeeling (attested 1995).
Ngawang Jorden is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He has held positions at Sakya College and served as director of the International Buddhist Academy.
